To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
microinjections of excitatory amino acids into specific hypothalamic sites in the cat elicit the jaw-opening component and the head-turning component of biting attack behaviour.

microinjections of the neurotransmitter glutamic acid into the perifornical hypothalamus of a cat elicited the jaw opening component of biting attack, and the results suggest that this component of biting attack is mediated by the activation of cell bodies in the perifornical region.

microinjections of the excitatory amino acid glutamate into a discrete site of the cat hypothalamus elicited the jaw opening component of biting attack behaviour; and that the glutamate-induced behaviour was not accompanied by other attack behaviours.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the neural mechanisms which mediate the behaviour of biting attack.
the identification of the neuronal systems involved in the expression of the aggressive behaviour of the cat.
the identification of the brain sites and neuronal systems which control the expression of aggressive behaviour, particularly biting.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
glutamate injections into the perifornical hypothalamus elicit the jaw-opening component, but not the biting, of attack behaviour.
biting attack in the cat is elicited from a population of perifornical hypothalamus neurones which are glutamate sensitive and are excited during the biting attack.
the biting attack is mediated by the perifornical hypothalamus and the ventral tegmental area of the midbrain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

(a) the hypothalamus and midbrain tegmentum are the major sites from which biting attack can be elicited by electrical or chemical stimulation, and (b) a major component of the behaviour is mediated by a population of hypothalamically projecting neurones.
the hypothalamus contains a number of cell groups which mediate the components of biting attack and that the perifornical area is the location of a group of cells mediating jaw opening.

(1), the perifornical hypothalamus contains neurones which are activated during the performance of biting attack; (2), the perifornically located neurones are activated by the hypothalamic defence area (HDA) which is the region of brain activated by electrical or chemical stimulation of the amygdala; (3), the perifornic neurones are activated during biting attack; and (4), the perifornice neurones are excited by glutamate and inhibited by glycine
The main takeaway from our work is that
we were able to identify a specific population of neurons in the hypothalamus that are involved in biting attack behavior in cats, and we were able to do this using glutamate injections.
glutamate injections into the hypothalamus can cause the animal to open their mouth, which is a key component of a biting attack.
we have identified a population of hypothalamus neurons that are necessary for the jaw opening component of biting attack behavior.
